title: GPU stack smoke matrix + validation walkthrough (lab notes)
content:
Purpose:
These lab notes capture a small, repeatable smoke validation matrix and a lightweight walkthrough for validating Kubernetes + GPU driver + CUDA + NCCL permutations on private (VPC/on-prem) clusters prior to formal rollout. This doc is intentionally concise: a set of quick-pass checks engineers can run in a new lab cluster or after a driver/OS/kernel upgrade to detect the common breakages we see in the field.

Scope and goals:
- Fast smoke checks (<30m) that exercise node driver loading, container runtime GPU visibility, basic inference kernels, and small NCCL all-reduce across 2 pods.
- Produce deterministic pass/fail outputs and a short log bundle to attach to tickets.
- Provide Terraform variable snippets used to provision the test cluster and notes on where to plug into our private-deployments modules.
- Capture common failure signatures and remediation steps.

Matrix (high-level):
- Kubernetes: 1.27, 1.26, 1.25
- Linux kernel: 5.15.x, 6.1.x, 6.4.x
- NVIDIA driver: 525.xx, 535.xx, 540.xx
- CUDA toolkit (in-container): 11.8, 12.1, 12.2
- NCCL: 2.15.x, 2.17.x
- Container runtime: containerd 1.7.x, docker-ce 24.x (note: docker engine is discouraged but sometimes present in customer labs)

Smoke tests (ordered):
1) Node sanity (host)
   - ssh to node -> sudo modinfo nvidia || dmesg | tail -n 80
   - expected: nvidia kernel modules listed, no WARN_ON/taint relevant to nvidia failure.
   - failure signature: "nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout" -> kernel module mismatch (driver vs kernel).

2) Driver visibility in container
   - run: docker run --gpus all --rm --entrypoint nvidia-smi nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi || 
     ctr run --rm --gpus all ... containerd example (see gist).
   - expected: GPUs shown, processes column empty or listing the test container.
   - failure signature: no devices or "No devices were found" -> CRI config / driver not exposed or wrong driver stack.

3) Simple CUDA warmup (inside container)
   - run: cuda-samples vectorAdd or a tiny python script that runs a few torch.cuda tensor ops (python snippet provided in gist).
   - expected: kernel runs, time < 2s for micro-bench on small data.
   - failure signature: CUDA driver version mismatch (CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN / driver versions printed).

4) NCCL local allreduce (single-node multi-GPU)
   - run NCCL tests (provided docker image) with 2 ranks on same node.
   - expected: allreduce completes without NCCL WARN or fatal.
   - failure signature: NCCL WARN on topology or incorrect NIC binding -> usually missing UCX or mxm config for RDMA.

5) NCCL cross-node allreduce (2 nodes, each 1 GPU)
   - requirement: multicast-free network, proper MTU, equivalently configured NICs.
   - run huggingface/allreduce test container from gist (script invokes mpirun with nccl).
   - expected: allreduce latency reported and no "NCCL WARN" per-rank.

6) Inference smoke (model load + 1 token generation)
   - pull small bert/gpt sample in a GPU-enabled pod. Run generation for 1 token.
   - expected: model loads into GPU memory and inference step completes.

Validation outputs to collect (script will tar these):
- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide (node-level distribution)
- kubectl describe node <node> and raw dmesg from node (last 200 lines)
- nvidia-smi -q (host) and from inside container
- /var/log/syslog or journalctl -k | grep -i nvidia (host)
- NCCL logs from test containers (stdout/stderr)
- Terraform plan and applied variables used for this run (vars.tfvars)

Example Terraform snippets (variables we set for test cluster):
- test_node_count = 2
- test_machine_type = "p4d.24xlarge" # or on-prem equivalent node label
- gpu_driver_version = "535.86.05"
- containerd_version = "1.7.6"
- kernel_version = "6.1.76"
- cuda_container_image = "nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-base"

(These get passed to modules/private-deployments/k8s-node-asg/main.tf in our infra repo. See linked PR for example variables.)

Quick troubleshooting checklist (ranked by frequency):
- Module mismatch: check uname -r vs installed nvidia kernel object (modinfo nvidia). If mismatch, rebuild or install matching driver.
- Driver install failed silently: check package manager logs (/var/log/dpkg.log or yum history). Some package repos drop meta packages.
- containerd config missing gpus support: verify /etc/containerd/config.toml has nvidia runtime and restart containerd.
- NCCL network errors: ensure TCP fallback is reachable; check iptables, ensure UDP/TCP ephemeral ports allowed, and MTU consistent across path.
- SELinux/AppArmor: sometimes blocks driver module loading or container device mounts—check audit logs.

Automated harness and scripts:
- quick_smoke.sh (bash) orchestrates node checks, runs the 6 smoke tests in order and collects artifacts into /tmp/gpu-smoke-<date>.tar.gz.
- smoke_runner.py (python) is a tiny runner that creates pods with GPU requests, retries on image pull backoff, and captures kubectl logs on failure. Gist link provides the two scripts.

Acceptance criteria for a pass:
- All 6 smoke tests return success status within the 30m window and the artifact bundle contains nvidia-smi outputs, kernel logs, and NCCL logs.
- No NCCL fatal errors and CUDA version printed matches the expected in-container runtime.
- Terraform re-provisioning is idempotent for the node pool variables used (no drift observed after apply -> plan shows no changes).

Known edge cases and notes from past runs:
- 540.xx drivers sometimes require a newer kernel backport on older distributions; record the distribution and packaging source when we see this.
- Some on-prem BIOS settings (SR-IOV / ACS) cause NVLink visibility differences; check vendor release notes for that exact server SKU.
- Docker legacy setups commonly hide containerd GPU support; prefer standardizing on containerd in our docs.

Rollout/upgrade plan (lightweight):
1) Run smoke matrix in lab with target driver/kernel/cuda combo.
2) If pass, schedule a canary pool (1-2 nodes) in the customer's dedicated cluster; run the same smoke harness via fluent job.
3) Promote to larger pool with staggered drain, run smoke checks on each drained/restarted node.
4) If failure at any step, rollback to previous node image/driver and attach tarball to Jira ticket.

Open TODOs (short):
- Add a small GPU-probing container image that contains all test binaries (nvidia-smi, cuda-samples, nccl-tests) to avoid network pulls in air-gapped labs.
- Wire quick_smoke.sh to our cluster-infra pipeline for automated periodic checks.
- Add a short video screencap template for operators to capture failing reproductions.

Appendix: sample kubectl commands used by the harness (copy-paste friendly)
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl describe node <node> | sed -n '1,200p' > node-desc.txt
- kubectl run -n test gpu-check --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-base -- /bin/bash -c "nvidia-smi && python3 /test-scripts/quick_cuda_test.py"
- docker run --gpus all --rm nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi

If you are running these tests and hit an unfamiliar failure, attach the artifact bundle to JIRA INF-2431 and ping #eng-private in slack with the short summary and timestamps.

----
Lab session notes (2026-02-24):
- Ran matrix on 2 baremetal nodes (Dell R7525) with kernel 6.1.76 + driver 535.86.05 + CUDA 12.1. Single-node and cross-node NCCL allreduce passed.
- Observed intermittent containerd image pull backoff in one node due to a flaky internal mirror (fixed by switching to alt registry).
- Action: create small atomized mirror for smoke images in private registry (see linked gist for image list).

End of notes.
